episodes.199388: A cold frontal boundary and mid-level shortwave moved across South Florida on March 25th bringing the potential for showers and isolated thunderstorms. When adding the Atlantic sea breeze and favorable conditions for strong winds and hail, the best potential for showers and storm was the east coast metropolitan area, especially Miami-Dade County.
episodes.200461: Scattered showers and storms developed along and ahead of a stalled boundary on Tuesday, March 25th into Wednesday, March 26th. Some storms produced severe hail in portions of North Texas, with the largest hail (2.25 inches) falling in Parker County early Wednesday morning.
episodes.200497: A weak upper system, moving along the periphery of a deeper upper low centered across Canada, fostered scattered hail-producing thunderstorms near the Red River from the evening of the 25th into the early morning of the 26th.
episodes.200568: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts and nickel size hail along the Treasure Coast.
episodes.200944: Rapid snowmelt due to warm temperatures caused the Silvies River to rise to 14.76 feet, about half a foot under the record of 15.2 feet. This caused significant flooding in and around Burns, Oregon while the river was in flood stage from March 25th through April 3rd and from April 10th through April 15th. Flooding was visible over the area between the two flood stage events and for a few days after April 15th.
